chunks: Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said, "I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:"

"Remain patient in obeying Allah, and remain patient in keeping away from disobeying Allah, for indeed this world is a short moment; that which has passed from it is [such that you find neither joy nor sorrow for it now, while that which has not yet come is] unknown to you, so remain patient in the present moment that you are in, and it will be as though you have been granted [its reward]."
ai.seo_question: How should one practice patience in this world according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) frames patience (*sabr*) as a dual discipline: active perseverance in obedience and passive endurance in avoiding sin, grounded in the transient nature of the world (*dunya*). By describing the present moment as a 'given hour' that has already been granted, the Imam emphasizes the immediacy of divine accounting, a concept deeply resonant with Shia eschatology where the brevity of life serves as a catalyst for spiritual readiness. This teaching underscores the practical application of *zuhd* (asceticism) not as withdrawal, but as mindful endurance within the temporal sphere.
